name: Intro to CoDesign & Proposal
sub: Before the Double Diamond · project framing
obj: Explain what CoDesign brings, understand the client's real challenge and turn it into a clear, tailored proposal.
who: Business/Sales brings the opportunity and commercial ambition · CoDesign team challenges the brief, selects the approach and writes the proposal · Client shares context, constraints and expected outcomes.
acc: CoDesign lead (N3) signs off the proposal; account owner validates commercial terms.
when: At the start of an opportunity, before the project is launched and before Discover. Prerequisite: 02.03 Client Intelligence brief.
inputs: Client brief or request; business context; stakeholders, timing, budget if known; relevant previous work. Minimum evidence: a named sponsor and a written brief (even an email).
steps: Understand the initial request and context
Reframe: challenge the problem as stated
output: A tailored proposal: challenge, objectives, approach, phases, activities, deliverables, stakeholders, timeline and budget.
std: A non-designer can read it and explain what will happen, why, and what the client receives.
quality: Client-specific, outcome-oriented, realistic; the method answers a real need.
mistakes: Selling a workshop when the problem needs research · copying a past proposal without reframing · promising outcomes that need user evidence.
handoff: Proposal accepted and a sponsor named → 03.01 Kick-off & Planning.
example: WORK: Northbridge asks for 'a workshop to fix the restaurant'. The team reframes it as 'make the anchor day worth the commute' and proposes Discover (3 weeks), a half-day Format A workshop and a test plan. [fictional]

var.PLAY: Riverside asks for 'faster kiosks'. Reframe around the half-time journey, including access needs.
var.HEAL: St Aldric asks for 'a new menu'. Reframe around choice timing and family involvement; flag clinical sign-off in scope.
var.LEARN: Lakeshore asks for 'cheaper meal plans'. Reframe around the commuter's 3-hour gap.

cred: Choose 2-3 from 02.02. Credential grid S06 slide 7 proves projects are referenced, not their impact.
tools: Proposal template · Double Diamond overview · Miro · PowerPoint
deck: [S03, slides 6-9] · [S05, slides 27-28] planning and 70/20/10 · [S06, slide 5] engagement triggers
prompt: Use Brief Challenger with the client email and Client Intelligence brief: 'Score this brief on readiness, list the 5 clarification questions to ask before quoting, and flag any walk-away signals.'
verify: Scope, price, dates and named credentials; remove any figure the client has not given.
fallback: Fill the proposal template section by section: Context → Why now → Challenge → Objectives → Approach → Activities → Deliverables → Timeline → Team.
l_obj: Reframe a client request into a CoDesign challenge statement and justify the proposed approach.
explain: Presales is not Discover. Its job is to decide what deserves to be explored and how.

templates.label: XP Design for Client — proposal template (SharePoint)

exercise.situation: A client asks for 'a one-day workshop to redesign our staff canteen menu'. Budget set, date booked.
questions: What is the client really asking for, and what might the real challenge be?
Which two questions would you ask before agreeing?
Would you propose the workshop as requested? If not, what instead, and how do you justify it commercially?

answer_key.sample_answer: Real challenge is likely participation or experience, not the menu. Questions: 'What would success look like in 6 months?' and 'What do you already know about why people do or do not use the canteen?'. Keep the date but propose 2-3 weeks of light Discover before it, so the workshop works on evidence.
answer_key.success_criteria: Challenge statement names a user, a moment and an outcome; justification links approach to risk avoided.

name: Credentials Examples
obj: Select the few credentials that prove we can solve this client's challenge.
who: Business/Sales shares the opportunity · CoDesign team selects and adapts the story · Client reacts to what resonates.
acc: CoDesign lead checks every claim against the credential source and confidentiality rules.
when: During Presales, once the challenge is understood.
inputs: Client context and challenge; credential library; previous deliverables. Minimum evidence: each credential has an approved source file.
steps: Understand what needs to be proven
Adapt the story to the client
output: A short tailored selection: challenge, approach, outputs and, where documented, impact.
std: Every proof point traces to an approved document; confidential details removed.
quality: Relevant over exhaustive, recent, visual, connected to the client's challenge.
mistakes: Showing 15 logos · quoting impact figures nobody can source · using a confidential client name without approval.
example: HEAL: for St Aldric, shortlist Clariane (dining model, care homes) and explain the transfer limits: care homes are not acute wards, so lead with the method and the resident journey, not the numbers. [credential listed in S06; impact figures to verify]

var.WORK: Microsoft and Santander for workplace dining; show the persona and roadmap outputs.
var.PLAY: Arsenal FC or Roland-Garros for matchday F&B; check which artifacts are approved.
var.LEARN: No verified education credential: use a cross-sector case and say so openly.

cred: A listing proves a project is referenced; it does not prove a deliverable or quantified impact exists.
prompt: No selection agent exists. Generic Claude prompt: 'From this credential list [paste], shortlist 3 for a [segment] client whose challenge is [x]. For each: why it is relevant, the one proof point to lead with, and what must be verified before use.'
verify: Every figure and client name against SharePoint; sharing permission.
fallback: Filter the credential grid by segment and challenge, then apply the 3 questions: relevant? sourced? shareable?
l_obj: Shortlist 3 credentials with an explicit relevance rationale and one sourced proof point each.
explain: Don't show everything we have done. Show what proves we can solve this client's challenge.

exercise.situation: You are pitching to a hospital group that wants to improve the patient meal experience. The library holds 40 credentials.
questions: On which criteria do you shortlist three?
Your strongest case is an airport lounge. Do you show it, and how?
For your best credential, which single proof point do you lead with?

answer_key.sample_answer: Criteria: similar user moment, similar constraint (safety, time), approved artifacts. Show the lounge as 'how we redesign a time-pressured service moment', not as a sector match. Lead with a method proof (journey + pilot) unless an impact figure is sourced.
answer_key.success_criteria: Shortlist justified on user moment and constraint, not on sector logo alone.

name: Client Intelligence
obj: Understand the client's context, priorities, stakeholders and signals before engaging further.
who: Business/Sales shares account knowledge · CoDesign team researches and formulates hypotheses · Internal experts add sector knowledge.
acc: Account owner validates facts; CoDesign lead validates hypotheses.
when: At the very start of Presales, before or alongside first meetings.
inputs: Account information, previous proposals, public reports, CRM notes. Minimum evidence: sources listed for every fact.
output: A concise Client Intelligence Brief: context, priorities, challenges, stakeholders, signals, hypotheses, questions to validate.
std: Facts and assumptions are visibly separated; 3 questions ready for the first meeting.
quality: Relevant, recent, actionable; analysis produces better questions.
mistakes: A 30-page dossier nobody reads · presenting assumptions as facts · skipping the account team.
handoff: Brief shared with Sales and used in 02.01.
example: WORK: Northbridge annual report mentions 'return-to-office cost discipline' [fictional]. Fact: real-estate budget frozen. Assumption: employees dislike the restaurant. Question: 'What would make Tuesday worth coming in for?'

var.PLAY: Riverside: season-ticket renewal rate, new stand opening, local transport works.
var.HEAL: St Aldric: patient experience scores, waste targets, nurse staffing pressure.
var.LEARN: Lakeshore: enrolment trends, commuter ratio, affordability commitments.

cred: Previous work with the same client or sector (search 02.02 library).
tools: Account documentation, annual reports, CRM/SharePoint, stakeholder map
prompt: 'Prepare a pre-Discovery briefing on [client] for a first meeting with [role]. Separate [EVIDENCE] from [ASSUMPTION], list stakeholders and 3 questions to ask.'
verify: Every fact has a source; nothing confidential from CRM pasted into external tools beyond approved use.
fallback: Use the 9-heading template: Who → Context → Priorities → Challenges → Stakeholders → Trends → Relationship → Opportunities → Questions.
l_obj: Sort statements into facts and assumptions and write 3 open meeting questions.
explain: Client Intelligence is not Discovery. It prepares Discovery.

templates.label: Project template root (SharePoint) — Client Intelligence brief template: MISSING, owner Gabriel

exercise.situation: You have 45 minutes to prepare a first meeting with the Head of Workplace of a global bank.
questions: Where do you look first, and for what?
Sort: they are cutting real-estate costs · employees dislike the current offer · the CEO mentioned hybrid work in the annual report.
Write the three questions you would ask.

answer_key.sample_answer: Fact: CEO mention in annual report (sourced). Assumptions: cost cutting (unless sourced), employee dislike (needs evidence). Good questions are open and about outcomes: 'What does a good office day look like for you?'
answer_key.success_criteria: Correct fact/assumption sort with a reason; questions are open, not leading.
